cevap: Shift4's FY2024 10-K (filed 2025-02-19) states in its 'Concentration Risk' accounting-policy note: the Company's merchant processing activity in North America is facilitated by ONE vendor. Shift4 believes that vendor maintains appropriate backup systems and alternative arrangements to avoid a significant disruption of processing in an unforeseen event. Related concentration: a majority of revenue comes from processing card transactions, and because Shift4 is not a 'member bank' in North America it relies on a sponsorship agreement with a single member bank. The agreement requires Shift4 to abide by the card networks' by-laws and regulations; if Shift4 breaches it, the bank sponsor may terminate, and Shift4 would then have 180 days to identify an alternative bank sponsor. So the FY2024 vendor concentration is single-vendor processing plus single sponsor-bank dependence.

From ABNB 10-K key-business-metrics tables (FY2023 10-K for 2022/2023; FY2024 10-K for 2023/2024): Nights and Experiences Booked 394M (2022), 448M (2023), 492M (2024). Gross Booking Value $63,212M (2022), $73,252M (2023), $81,784M (2024). GBV per Night and Experience Booked = GBV / nights: 2022 = 63,212/394 = ~$160.4; 2023 = 73,252/448 = ~$163.5; 2024 = 81,784/492 = ~$166.2. That is roughly +1.9% in 2023 and +1.7% in 2024, i.e. modest ADR/mix-driven growth. 2024 FY2024 10-K commentary: revenue +12% to $11.1B on a 10% rise in nights plus higher Average Daily Rate driving a 12% GBV increase.

Production at the McCalla, Alabama facility was expected to begin during 2025. Per J.M. Smucker's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended April 30, 2024, filed 2024-06-18): in November 2021 Smucker announced plans to invest $1.1 billion to build a new manufacturing facility and distribution center in McCalla, Alabama dedicated to Smucker's Uncrustables frozen sandwiches; construction began in 2022, 'with production expected to begin in 2025.' The Properties footnote repeats: 'Production is expected to begin at the McCalla facility during 2025,' noting it complements existing Longmont, Colorado and Scottsville, Kentucky facilities. The later FY2026 10-K lists McCalla as an operating frozen-sandwich plant, confirming start-up.

The closest reported figure is Salesforce's FY2025 10-K (FYE January 31, 2025, filed March 5, 2025). Total outstanding principal of debt was $8,500 million (no revolver borrowings; the $5.0B credit facility was undrawn). The 2028 Senior Sustainability Notes (issued July 2021, 1.50%, due July 2028) had $1,000 million outstanding principal. Excluding those, face value = $7,500 million ($7.5 billion), comprised of: 2028 Senior Notes 3.70% $1,500M; 2031 Senior Notes 1.95% $1,500M; 2041 Senior Notes 2.70% $1,250M; 2051 Senior Notes 2.90% $2,000M; 2061 Senior Notes 3.05% $1,250M. The 2024 Senior Notes ($999M carrying) were repaid in full in Q2 FY2025.

Paylocity's FY2024 10-K (FYE June 30, 2024) groups these under 'Governmental Regulation' and 'Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters': (1) Changing regulatory requirements - tax, benefit, wage-and-hour and employment law changes may force product redesign, raise costs, delay launches, or eliminate demand; new/reinterpreted state and federal money transmitter / money services business statutes could require licensing or limit activities, hurting interest income on client funds, with civil and criminal fines if deemed an unlicensed money transmitter. (2) AI/machine learning - evolving US, EU and other AI legislation, potential IP, privacy, employment and civil-rights claims, regulatory scrutiny and fines. (3) Data privacy - HIPAA, GDPR (fines up to 4% of worldwide revenue), CCPA/CPRA, BIPA, state breach-notification laws; rising enforcement actions and reputational damage. (4) Adverse tax laws - sales/use tax on electronically delivered services, possibly retroactive, plus past-tax, interest and penalty exposure. (5) Litigation risk generally.

Microsoft's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024) states: 'As of June 30, 2024, we employed approximately 228,000 people on a full-time basis, 126,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally.' So the share of full-time employees located outside the United States is 102,000 / 228,000 = approximately 44.7% (about 45%); the U.S. share is 126,000 / 228,000 = approximately 55.3%. For context the same disclosure splits the total by function: 86,000 in operations (product support, consulting, datacenter operations, manufacturing and distribution), 81,000 in product research and development, 45,000 in sales and marketing, and the remainder in general and administration.

Allstate's FY2024 10-K (Note 14, Capital Structure) shows $500 million outstanding of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures (listed as 'due 2067'). Terms: scheduled maturity May 15, 2057, final maturity May 15, 2067. Interest is payable semi-annually at the fixed 6.500% rate to May 15, 2037, then quarterly at three-month LIBOR plus 2.120%, replaced by CME Term SOFR (3-month) plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment. Redeemable in whole or part on/after May 15, 2037 at principal plus accrued interest, or earlier in certain circumstances at principal plus accrued interest or, if greater, a make-whole price. Allstate may defer interest for consecutive periods up to 10 years (interest compounds); during deferral it cannot pay dividends or repurchase common/preferred. 75 million authorized unissued common shares are reserved for the deferral obligation. A replacement capital covenant applies, with the $800M 2053 Subordinated Debentures as covered debt.

Netflix's FY2024 10-K (as of December 31, 2024) discloses material cash requirements from known contractual obligations due in the Next 12 Months (i.e. 2025) of $14,426,266 thousand, about $14.4 billion. Components: content obligations $11,424,696K (~$11.4B), debt (principal plus interest) $2,486,945K (~$2.5B), and operating lease obligations $514,625K (~$0.5B). Total obligations across all periods were $45,851,513K (~$45.9B), with $31,425,247K beyond 12 months. Netflix notes the table excludes unknown future-title content obligations, which it believes could total roughly $1-4 billion over the next three years, with the vast majority payable after the next twelve months.

Snap's FY2024 10-K does not print a single 'maximum dilution' figure, but it gives principal outstanding at 12/31/2024 and each initial conversion rate (shares per $1,000 principal): 2025 Notes $36.240M at 46.1233 = ~1.67M shares; 2026 Notes $249.754M at 43.8481 = ~10.95M; 2027 Notes $1,150M at 11.2042 = ~12.88M; 2028 Notes $1,500M at 17.7494 = ~26.62M; 2030 Notes $750M at 45.0846 = ~33.81M. Total principal $3,685.994M implies approximately 85.9 million Class A shares maximum at initial conversion rates (rates can rise on make-whole fundamental changes/redemption). Capped calls on the 2026-2030 Notes (cap prices $32.58/$121.02/$93.90/$33.48) offset dilution above the conversion price up to the cap; the 2025 capped calls were terminated in May 2024. All were out-of-the-money and if-converted value did not exceed principal at 12/31/2024.
